title: When the Shabad takes the mind in hand
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 221
summary: The shabad begins with a startling image: the mind as elephant, the Guru as goad, the Shabad as the mark that disciplines it. It carries the listener through the failure of cleverness and the growth of fearlessness, then settles in daily remembrance of the One already pervading everything.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose mind is strong, clever, and difficult to govern. Taken steadily, it changes what authority feels like: wit, image, and force stop leading, and the Guru's word takes the mind in hand.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: let the Guru's Shabad govern the mind before cleverness does.

lines.translation: Gauree Gwaarayree, First Mehla:
The mind is an elephant in the forest of the body.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰੁ ਅੰਕਸੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਬਦੁ ਨੀਸਾਨੈ ॥ ਰਾਜ ਦੁਆਰੈ ਸੋਭ ਸੁ ਮਾਨੈ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: gur a(n)kas sach sabadh neesaanai || raaj dhuaarai sobh su maanai ||1||
lines.translation: The Guru is the controlling stick; when the Insignia of the True Shabad is applied, one obtains honor in the Court of God the King. ||1||
He cannot be known through clever tricks.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਨੁ ਮਾਰੇ ਕਿਉ ਕੀਮਤਿ ਪਾਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: bin maare kiau keemat pai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Without subduing the mind, how can His value be estimated? ||1||Pause||
In the house of the self is the Ambrosial Nectar, which is being stolen by the thieves.
No one can say no to them.
He Himself protects us, and blesses us with greatness. ||2||
There are billions, countless billions of fires of desire at the seat of the mind.
They are extinguished only with the water of understanding, imparted by the Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਦੇ ਲੀਆ ਰਹਸਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਈ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: man dhe leeaa rahas gun gaiee ||3||
lines.translation: Offering my mind, I have attained it, and I joyfully sing His Glorious Praises. ||3||
Just as He is within the home of the self, so is He beyond.
But how can I describe Him, sitting in a cave?
The Fearless Lord is in the oceans, just as He is in the mountains. ||4||
Tell me, who can kill someone who is already dead?
What does he fear? Who can frighten the fearless one?
He recognizes the Word of the Shabad, throughout the three worlds. ||5||
One who speaks, merely describes speech.
But one who understands, intuitively realizes.
Seeing and reflecting upon it, my mind surrenders. ||6||
Praise, beauty and liberation are in the One Name.
In it, the Immaculate Lord is permeating and pervading.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਬਿਆਪਿ ਰਹਿਆ ਨਿਜ ਠਾਈ ॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: nij ghar biaap rahiaa nij Thaiee ||7||
lines.translation: He dwells in the home of the self, and in His own sublime place. ||7||
The many silent sages lovingly praise Him.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਨਿ ਮਨਿ ਸੂਚੈ ਸਾਚੁ ਸੁ ਚੀਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: tan man soochai saachu su cheet ||
lines.translation: Their bodies and minds are purified, as they enshrine the True Lord in their consciousness.
O Nanak, meditate on the Lord, each and every day. ||8||2||

structure: First, it starts with restraint, not self-display: the mind needs the Guru's goad and the Shabad's mark.
Then, it strips away cleverness and fear, teaching that freedom comes when the mind is no longer trying to rule itself.
Finally, it ends in daily remembrance of the Lord who already pervades the whole field.
